title.description: What it's for, in a few plain words a person reads at a glance, e.g. "Verify the browser_tab_groups.js fix" or "Re-check the backed-out tab notes patch": no job names, counts or reasons (those go in purpose).

purpose.description: One line: what this push answers.

tryArgs.description: The arguments after `./mach try`, selector first, e.g. ["fuzzy", "-q", "'xpcshell 'linux", "--rebuild", "10"].

scope.description: stack: a large push checking the whole stack is ready (first verification, last one before review). fixes: targeted, only what specific fixes need, typically for what failed on an earlier push. debug: to get logs or profiles.

feedback.description: Problems with the tools or inputs you used, one entry per problem.

regressions.description: Only when the stack was pushed before: each failure of that push the stack caused, and the patch whose change since then claims to fix it.

failure.description: The failure in one line: its tests, configs and message.

causedBy.description: The id of the patch that broke it.

fixedBy.description: The id of the patch whose change since that push fixes it; absent if nothing does.

how.description: What that change does about it, from its interdiff; or why nothing fixes it yet.

status.description: fixed: a change since that push fixes it (fixedBy). patch removed: the patch that caused it is no longer in the stack. pre-existing: shown failing the same way on central (cite it in how). not fixed: none of these.

answer.description: Only when revising after the user's comment: what you changed and why, in one or two sentences; if you couldn't do what they asked, say so and why.
